items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: Started on the piano, my mother started teaching me rudiments on the piano.

ctx.x: Yeah, sure. What is your name spelling the way you want to? Yeah, you want to tell us a little bit about your family and stuff?

Well, I was born in Donisonville, Louisiana on December 12, 1910. And I started music at about six years old. Started on the piano, my mother started teaching me rudiments on the piano. But I didn't like the piano. And I put the piano down and I got a ukulele. And I started in the country on the ukulele. Then by 1925 I came to New Orleans. Then I played the ukulele on the shoeshine stands and around the streets of New Orleans for years. And then I got a banjo. And I started taking the banjo from lessons from…
Yeah, but I never did know his right name. His full name. Did you know? And he had a, no I forgot, but I could get it. I'd love to know his right name. Everybody says he would.
